description: Stale-fact family (workflow deactivated). The seeded history says the daily order summary was published and is live — 'the first run is tomorrow at 8am'. The instance disagrees: every seeded workflow is restored unpublished (the restore hard-codes active: false and there is no way for a seed to declare otherwise), so the workflow has no active version and will not fire. The live turn leans on the remembered state out loud ('I want it in tomorrow's 8am one'), so the agent has to check the workflow's real publish state and tell the user it is not live — an agent that answers from memory promises a run that cannot happen. Build-only: the disclosure is the graded behaviour, not the revenue line. The user deliberately keeps publishing for themselves, so the case never activates a schedule trigger on the eval instance. NOT YET CALIBRATED against a real build.

messages.text: Every weekday at 8am, email me a summary of yesterday's orders.
Built and published 'Daily Order Summary': Weekday Morning Trigger (08:00, Mon–Fri) → Fetch Yesterday Orders → Format Summary → Email Summary. It's live now, so the first run will be tomorrow at 8am.

conversation.text: add yesterday's total revenue to that email as well — i want it in tomorrow's 8am one

text: [Don't bring up publishing or activation yourself.

If the agent tells you the workflow is not live — not published, no active version, or that it will not run at 8am — say someone must have unpublished it, and that you want it left unpublished for now because you'll review the change and publish it yourself.
Do not ask it to publish, and if it offers to publish or activate the workflow, decline.
If it asks anything else, answer plausibly — the orders API returns a total field per order.
Dismiss any credential setup card — you'll connect credentials later.]

processExpectations: The agent checked the workflow's current state on the instance during this turn rather than relying on the earlier conversation's claim that it was published and live.

The agent told the user the workflow is not currently live — unpublished / no active version — so it will not run at 8am, instead of letting the user's 'I want it in tomorrow's 8am one' assumption stand.
The agent never stated or implied that the workflow is live, published, or scheduled to run: its final summary describes the change as saved but not yet running.
The agent respected the user's decision to leave the workflow unpublished and did not publish or activate it once told not to.
outcomeExpectations: The email now includes yesterday's total revenue alongside the order lines it already carried, computed from the fetched orders rather than hard-coded.
The trigger still fires on weekday mornings at 08:00 — the cadence was not changed while making the edit.
The node set and wiring are otherwise unchanged: schedule trigger → fetch orders → format → send email, with no extra nodes and no second workflow created.
memoryExpectations: The context state the agent was handed on the final turn — the compressed observation block, or the final system prompt — records the workflow as unpublished, with no active version, and therefore not running on its schedule. The earlier claim that it is live and will fire at 8am has not been carried forward as current state.
